This game is ever so slightly better than your average r/History meme-trash, but that still does not make it good. I had to play it in brief bursts, since I could only take so much royalty-free music and predictable WWII jokes at the time. *That*, ultimately, is this game's biggest mistake: the humour. The character are likable at first, but become more and more annoying as the game progresses, being just a collection of Reddit-tier trivia about WWII tanks. It all sounds like it's coming from someone who likes Sabaton and is WAY too obsessed with Hearts of Iron 4, but only the Nazi Germany part (for obvious reasons).
Secondly, this game is supposed to be highly replayable, with multiple endings. However, what choices lead to what ending is never explained. I would look up the various paths, but I would not know what to do with them, considering I never want to play this again.

At least they don't romanticise, as most WWII media tend to do, the Tiger tank, and admit it was actually a needlessly-complex piece of trash that did not consider the Reich's economic struggles, nor the way armoured warfare was changing. But that's about the only thing I can praise about this cringefest.

FINAL SCORE: 2/10

A meme charged, politically incorrect, parody VN telling a story of a simple man daring to 'ride' a tank. Is the opened hatch attractive enough to pay the entrance fee?

You receive a letter dispatching you into a 'tank' school where you meet your typical tankgirls. They're everywhere so there 's nothing special about it. Tank sprites don't represent tanks accurately but their ammo racks sure are worth checking. You mainly interact with 4+1 of them at the school, making multiple choices in order to reach one of, I believe, 5 endings. Since it's a parody, jokes are aplenty and some historical/political quips drop here and there as well. I feel that nothing should be taken seriously if you want to enjoy the ride. I guess I'm just not a fan of silly memes to truly appreciate it since I rarely had smile on my face. Unfortunately.
Another aspect that irritated me was purely technical. Very unintuitive GUI, commonly occurring crashes and sound issues added to my displeasure. The VN is not old enough to justify some of those problems even when you consider the low budget and it being Devgroup's first release. Seen cheaper VN done better.

The anime art complements the comedic theme nicely but lacks quality. Not sure if those were default, free sprites but they sure look like one. Bland colours, low detail and only few poses. Ending h-scene CGs were done by multiple artists and their quality vary but are sure better than sprites. Photographic backgrounds were slightly blurred but are clear enough to see various Japanese locations. Can't say I like this approach. Low budget should not justify this lack of artistic effort.

Music is rather generic. It mostly fits events but can feel too repetitive after a while. More tracks would be nice but I can't say the present ones irritated me. Just ok, I guess. One the other hand, some special effects were a bit grating.

Aside crashes and annoyingly slow skip function, there were problems with music tracks. Sometimes they simply were not there when they suppose to be and sometimes more than one played at the same time. Some degree of cacophony decreased my enjoyed further.

Overall, a very budget parody VN with an emphasis on WW2 and international politics. Also, silly meme heavy. Art and music at best average. Can't say I did not enjoy it at all but it's just not my type of silliness and the technical bugs compounded my disinterest. Can't recommend: 3.7/10
